evidence: Clear separation of concerns into domain-agnostic modules: downloader/, parser/, writer/, with internal cohesion (e.g., multiple parser subclasses inheriting from common Parser base class)
Shared domain model (User, Weibo classes in weibo_spider/) used across modules, indicating tight coupling within the same process space
Single entry point (__main__.py → spider.main) orchestrating the flow, but with modular internal structure

No explicit inter-service communication patterns (e.g., HTTP clients to external services beyond the target API, no message broker usage beyond optional adapters like KafkaWriter which are pluggable implementations within same process)
Package dependency fan-out is low to moderate (avg_fan_out ≈ 3), consistent with modular monolith where modules depend on a few core interfaces
Inheritance hierarchy (e.g., Downloader → ImgDownloader → *PictureDownloader; Parser → *Parser; Writer → *Writer) reflects modular abstraction within one runtime
Test structure (tests/ top-level, parallel to source) confirms standard Python project layout with internal module testing, not distributed system testing
risks: Monolithic deployment and scaling — cannot independently scale components
Tight domain coupling may emerge as more output targets (writers) or parsing logic evolve
No strict boundary enforcement between modules (e.g., writer modules may indirectly depend on parser internals via Weibo/User classes), risking gradual architectural drift
